industry.headline: UK moves ahead on under-16 social media restrictions under Children's Wellbeing and Schools Act
industry.summary: UK confirms its under-16 social media ban is proceeding via new Section 214A powers in the Online Safety Act, with enforcement beginning Spring 2027, Ofcom overseeing age-assurance standards, and penalties up to 10% of global revenue. Directly relevant to NOMO's active UK pilot and CEO Leonardo's policy engagement ahead of enforcement.

industry.headline: Social media addiction litigation and settlements accelerate across US states and France
industry.source: Robert King Law Firm (legal industry tracker)
industry.summary: 51 state AGs reached a $17.1B settlement with Meta over youth harm claims, France's parliament approved a under-15 social media account ban, and Boston sued Meta, ByteDance, Snap and Google over addictive design targeting minors. Signals a funding and compliance tailwind for NOMO's school-partnership pitch in its priority US market.

industry.headline: Connecticut AG opens investigation into messaging app Kik, citing Meta settlement precedent
industry.summary: CT AG Tong opened a formal probe into Kik's age-verification and moderation practices, explicitly invoking the $17.1B Meta settlement as precedent; CT will receive $266.1M from that deal, with at least half earmarked for youth-harm remediation — a potential funding channel for digital-wellbeing programs like NOMO.

reconsider.name: Yondr
reconsider.reason: Hardware phone-pouch/implementation vendor, not a software/app-based competitor — mismatched with NOMO's established competitor set (Opal, Brick, Forest, etc.).
reconsider.why_fits: Yondr dominates the K-12 phone-free implementation market that NOMO's 6-12 Education vertical targets directly, with large contracts in exactly the districts NOMO would pursue (LAUSD, NYC, Chicago). Yondr operates in all 50 US states plus has offices in London and Sydney, overlapping NOMO's US/UK/AU GTM priorities.

reconsider.name: S'moresUp
reconsider.reason: Medium confidence; duplicative chore/screen-time reward mechanic already covered by other selected candidates.
reconsider.why_fits: S'moresUp ties earned points directly to screen time and rewards, functioning as a reward-for-behavior competitor: <cite index="43-1,43-2">kids earn points for completing chores, and those points can be exchanged for screen time, allowance, or custom rewards, with a goal-setting feature for longer-term objectives</cite>.

reconsider.category: K-12 digital wellness curriculum / school partnerships
reconsider.name: Screen Guardians
reconsider.reason: Curriculum-based model rather than an app/product competitor; weak fit against the app-block competitor bar.
reconsider.why_fits: Screen Guardians provides K-12 curriculum and school-facing digital wellness programming, positioning it as a direct rival for the same school/district partnership budgets and mindshare NOMO targets in its 6-12 Education GTM vertical, even though its model is education-based rather than app-based.

reconsider.name: Museum of Ice Cream
reconsider.reason: Overlaps with existing partner Fever's museum-ticket coverage; weak differentiation as a new reward category, and its comparison to a nonexistent 'McDonald's' partner in NOMO's lineup is inaccurate.
reconsider.why_fits: Museum of Ice Cream runs teen/Gen-Z-friendly experiential locations offering free-entry style promos (e.g. <cite index="20-5">Museum of Ice Cream (IL, NY, TX): visit for FREE Ice Cream, FREE sprinkle pool, unique swag, and more</cite>), combining the exact 'museum tickets' plus novelty ice-cream reward combo NOMO already likes (per its McDonald's ice-cream cone tie-in), and is not yet in NOMO's partner roster.

reconsider.name: TeenTix
reconsider.reason: Overlaps with existing partner Fever, which already covers museum tickets — not a differentiated reward category.
reconsider.why_fits: TeenTix is a teen-specific ticket network offering $5 admission to museums, theatre, dance, and visual arts across partner venues, filling exactly the 'museum tickets' gap in NOMO's reward lineup with an audience and price point built specifically for teens.

reconsider.name: Culture Pass (NYC public libraries)
reconsider.reason: Redundant category already covered by TeenTix and existing partner Fever; narrow single-city scope.
reconsider.why_fits: Culture Pass is a teen-eligible (13+) municipal-adjacent rewards inventory source: it is "a program for cardholding patrons 13 and older of Brooklyn Public Library, New York Public Library and Queens Public Library" that lets New Yorkers "reserve a pass and get free admission to dozens of NYC cultural institutions, including museums." This mirrors NOMO's museum-ticket/city-pass reward category (like GetYourGuide/Fever) but is not currently in NOMO's partner lineup, and its library/city backing also gives it secondary relevance as a Municipalities GTM entry point.

reconsider.name: City of Dallas Teen All-Access Pass (Dallas Park and Recreation Dept.)
reconsider.reason: Duplicate of the City of Dallas Parks & Recreation Teen All-Access Pass candidate covering the same program; kept the more detailed entry instead.
reconsider.why_fits: Dallas relaunched its Teen All-Access Pass, giving 25,000 youth ages 13-17 free access to recreational and cultural attractions through city-brokered partnerships with local organizations, mirroring the Municipalities GTM vertical NOMO is pursuing for direct city partnerships.

reconsider.name: Health insurer / wellness-app partnership trend (sector signal)
reconsider.reason: Generic industry survey statistic, not a named/concrete prospect; redundant with the more concrete Elevance Health/Anthem candidate already covering the Insurance vertical.
reconsider.why_fits: Recent industry polling confirms strong near-term appetite among health insurers for exactly the kind of partnership NOMO could offer: "41.1% of respondents identified partnerships between health insurers and mental health and wellness apps as the most important non-traditional partnership over the next three years," reinforcing that Insurance remains an underexploited vertical for NOMO given it has no GTM partners there yet.

reconsider.why_fits: Horry County Schools launched a new 'Protected Learning' initiative with grade-specific daily screen time guidelines in classrooms, showing an active district need for a screen-time management/rewards partner.

rejected_today.why_fits: Kikaroo lets teens earn points toward rewards like screen time, cash, or outings for completing chores, positioning it as a gamified-reward alternative competing for the same teen habit-change use case.

rejected_today.why_fits: Illinois just signed a statewide law requiring bell-to-bell cellphone restrictions in public schools starting 2027-2028, creating a fresh, large-scale procurement need for implementation partners across the state's districts.
